source.title: On the Convergence and Robustness of Batch Normalization
source.authors: Yong-Qiang Cai; Qian-Xiao Li; Zuo-Wei Shen

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices. Its title differs from the catalog title: the text is “A Quantitative Analysis of the Effect of Batch Normalization on Gradient Descent.”
record.tranche_reason: Compares batch-normalized gradient descent with ordinary gradient descent and reports early-epoch loss and learning-rate stability in supervised learning experiments. The neural-network experiments use different measures and settings from the claim’s cited BN studies.
record.gate_note: The paper’s OLS convergence results are not benchmark classification results. Neural-network experiments report loss at the first epoch and, in one separate MNIST width experiment, accuracy at the first epoch; these do not measure training classification error or zero error. Figure 3 tests scaling behavior and is not a BN-versus-no-BN comparison. Reported values in Figures 3–4 are not recoverable from the supplied text, so only explicitly described comparisons are recorded as figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares BN and no-BN neural networks across learning rates. First-epoch loss provides evidence about optimization speed, and instability across learning rates tests V6's tolerance component. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish convergence, conditional linear acceleration, and learning-rate robustness for OLS, then report that selected properties extend qualitatively, and sometimes quantitatively, to neural-network experiments. They do not establish these guarantees generally for deep networks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses batch normalization and compares with GD, but reports early-epoch loss and stability in small networks on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 rather than the accuracy-speed settings and architectures named in V6.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that BN accelerates convergence more for deep than one-layer networks. Stability depends on using separate learning rates for BN parameters and other parameters; shared rates show a maximum allowed learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: For OLS, BNGD converges for arbitrary weight learning rates when the BN scale rate lies in (0,1]; global convergence for almost all initializations is proved when that rate equals 1. Conditional linear convergence and acceleration are also established and numerically examined.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN reparameterization can improve convergence and learning-rate robustness in ordinary least-squares regression.

fits_no_version.finding: BNGD's learning-rate insensitivity interval grows approximately with dimension in OLS and with hidden-layer width in the MNIST experiment; the latter lacks a no-BN comparator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing width can broaden the useful learning-rate range of batch-normalized networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Rescaling initial non-BN parameters and learning rates produces approximately matching early-training curves, with deviations when the normalization epsilon becomes significant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-normalized training approximately obeys a weight-scale and learning-rate scaling law.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 97, 2019
record.problems: Neural-network results characterize performance at the first epoch, before models have generally converged. The plotted values are not numerically stated in the supplied text, and no error bars are stated for the reported five-run averages.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The Section 4.2 MNIST width experiment reports accuracy at the first epoch for stochastic BNGD, but does not compare BN with a no-BN baseline and does not show the behavior named in V6.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the specified CIFAR model-size and training-recipe comparisons.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and training very deep plain or residual networks.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence from initially subthreshold rates.
Accuracy gains over training, performance through convergence, the named sigmoid/VGG/Inception settings, and Fixup's speed and stability without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports qualitative verdicts without reconstructing Figure 4 values. First-epoch loss bears on optimization speed but does not directly measure accuracy speed or eventual training error. A missing numerical transcription is not evidence that an effect is partial.

versions.untested_parts: No training classification error, corrupted or random labels, or model-size comparison for CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or width sweep.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison or training-error results.
Uses Glorot initialization in neural-network experiments but does not compare initializations or test signal propagation or trainable depth.
No test of recovery above a stability threshold, sharpness tracking, or the stated full-batch squared-loss settings.

Tests BN versus GD on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10, using loss at the first epoch; it does not test VGG on CIFAR-10 or Inception on ImageNet, nor report accuracy-speed comparisons for these experiments. It also does not test Fixup.
